title: localStorage, sessionStorage, storage events
learningObjectives: Explain localstorage, sessionstorage, storage events and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: Web Storage stores string key-value pairs. localStorage persists across browser sessions; sessionStorage is scoped to a page session and browsing context. The storage event notifies other documents sharing the relevant storage area when a value changes; it does not fire in the document that made the change.
understand.whyItMatters: Storage is convenient for non-sensitive preferences but is not a secure vault or a permanent database. Handle unavailable storage and malformed data.
understand.analogy: Storage is a small browser-side notebook; the storage event tells other open pages when a note changes.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The listener runs in other same-origin documents that share the storage area, not in the tab that performed the write.

examples.explanation: The listener runs in other same-origin documents that share the storage area, not in the tab that performed the write.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Open two same-origin tabs. Change a preference in one and update the other tab when its storage event fires.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Does the storage event fire in the same document that calls localStorage.setItem()?
questions.explanation: The storage event is dispatched to other documents sharing the storage area.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
